extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and establishments; agency managers responsible for Federal employee parking
extracted.subtask_description: A draft Office of Management and Budget circular proposing policy, pricing, and implementation requirements for Federal employee parking (fees, carpooling/vanpooling plans, phase-in) and soliciting agency comments. It sets standards for when and how agencies should charge for or manage parking to encourage transit and reduce single-occupant vehicle use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation for written comments and comment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Attached for your review is a draft circular ... We invite your written comments and ask that they be sent to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, Room 9202, OMB, Washington, D.C. 20503, no later than April 30, 1979.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for stakeholder input on the draft; comments must be mailed to the named official by the specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fees for the use of certain government parking lots
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular is intended to establish fees for the use of certain government parking lots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General policy objective to move from subsidized parking toward charging users; applies to 'certain' Federal parking lots (further scope clarified elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee basis: fair monthly rental value of the parking space
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees should reflect commercial rental-equivalent values (i.e., market/fair rental value) rather than arbitrary nominal amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum threshold exemption ($10 per month)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except that in most cases no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $10.00 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative carve-out to avoid charging trivial amounts; implementation detail setting a floor under which parking remains free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee design balance: recover costs and incentivize carpooling without being administratively consumed
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to set a fee high enough to recover space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee-setting should balance policy incentives and practical administrative costs; avoid fees too small to justify collection costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period for adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation should include transitional timing/measures so affected employees and agencies can adapt (e.g., arrange carpools, adjust budgets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative plans required where parking continues to be provided without charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency managers at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge will be required to develop and implement affirmative plans for maximizing carpooling and vanpooling among employees and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where agencies retain free parking, they must proactively plan and implement measures to maximize shared rides (carpools, vanpools) — a mandatory management obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stricter application of carpooling requirements across locations
rubrics_metrics.description: More stringent application of carpooling requirements will affect all locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy anticipates tightening enforcement/requirements for carpool utilization government-wide, not just in certain sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary effect targeted to downtown and densely populated suburban locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown locations and densely populated suburban locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope guidance: expect commercial-rate charging and related management where market parking alternatives and congestion justify intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objectives: reduce single-occupant vehicles, conserve energy, reduce congestion, improve air quality, increase transit and carpooling, and save costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerable cost savings to the taxpayer, reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use, greater carpooling and improved air quality are expected from this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the explicit goals used to justify the parking fee and carpooling measures; evaluations of policy success should measure these outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical justification from regional studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on studies which relate automobile use to the cost of parking, the Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments concluded charging commercially equivalent fees would reduce the number of cars in the core; a Los Angeles comparative study supports that user-pays parking increases carpooling and transit use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy is supported by cited evidence; agencies should consider these studies when assessing expected impacts and when designing local implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity consideration between employees who receive subsidized Federal parking and those who pay commercial rates
rubrics_metrics.description: About 42 percent of the Federal employees in downtown Washington... are able to park in Federal lots and thus receive a subsidy for part of the cost of their trip to work compared to other Federal employees who take transit or park in commercial parking and pay out-of-pocket costs along with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale highlights fairness concerns; policy aims to remove cross-subsidies that advantage some Federal employees over others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that commercial-rate charging will not impose hardship due to sharing or transit options
rubrics_metrics.description: In the vast majority of cases, charging a commercial-rate for parking is not expected to impose a hardship. In many cases employees will be able to share the costs through carpooling; in other cases, public transit may be a more cost effective option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation planning should assume mitigation via carpooling/transit; agencies may provide information or facilitation to help employees transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for uniform application and enforcement of carpooling regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: A GSA survey conducted in 1977 at OMB's request shows that government-wide carpooling regulations are not uniformly applied; e.g., over a third of executive branch parking spaces in the DC core were still used by single occupant vehicles despite a 90 percent utilization objective by carpools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy implies agencies must improve compliance and uniform enforcement of carpooling rules; evaluations should check for consistent application.
